definitions.explanation: The stone monument placed at a grave, usually inscribed with the family name or a Buddhist posthumous name. The standard formal term in Japan.

examples.japanese: {墓石|ぼせき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{彫|ほ}ってある→彫る：00114_horu⟧。
examples.english: The name is engraved on the gravestone.

examples.japanese: {墓石|ぼせき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{磨|みが}いて→磨く：02427_migaku⟧⟦{掃除|そうじ}→掃除：02889_souji⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I polished and cleaned the gravestone.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{彼岸|ひがん}→お彼岸：08933_ohigan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦お{墓|はか}{参|まい}り→お墓参り：15303_ohakamairi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}き→行く：00119_iku⟧、{墓石|ぼせき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かけて→かける：00854_kakeru⟧⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{合|あ}わせた→合わせる：01872_awaseru⟧。
examples.english: During the equinox week, my family visited the grave, poured water on the gravestone, and joined our hands in prayer.

examples.japanese: ⟦{近年|きんねん}→近年：14349_kinnen⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{樹木|じゅもく}→樹木：04955_jumoku⟧{葬|そう}⟦など→〜など：03095_nado⟧、{墓石|ぼせき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{建|た}てない→建てる：01189_tateru⟧⟦{形式|けいしき}→形式：00211_keishiki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦お{墓|はか}→お墓：21734_ohaka⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{増|ふ}えている→増える：01183_fueru⟧。
examples.english: In recent years, alternative grave styles such as tree burials, which do not involve a traditional gravestone, have been increasing.

notes:
{墓石|ぼせき} combines {墓|ぼ} (grave) and {石|せき} (stone), forming a Sino-Japanese compound for the gravestone or tombstone. It is the standard formal term, used in news, funeral industry contexts, and everyday speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {墓石|ぼせき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{建|た}てる→建てる：01189_tateru⟧: to erect a gravestone
- {墓石|ぼせき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{磨|みが}く→磨く：02427_migaku⟧: to polish a gravestone
- {墓石|ぼせき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かける→かける：00854_kakeru⟧: to pour water on a gravestone (standard part of grave-visiting in Japan)
- {墓石|ぼせき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{彫|ほ}る→彫る：00114_horu⟧: to engrave a name on a gravestone
- {墓石|ぼせき}⟦{業者|ぎょうしゃ}→業者：13130_gyousha⟧: gravestone dealer / mason

CULTURAL NOTE:
- Traditional Japanese gravestones are usually rectangular polished granite columns. The family name is engraved on the front, and the side often lists the posthumous Buddhist names ({戒名|かいみょう}) and dates of those buried there.
- Grave visits during ⟦お{彼岸|ひがん}→お彼岸：08933_ohigan⟧ (the equinox weeks) and ⟦お{盆|ぼん}→お盆：05587_obon⟧ (Bon festival) typically include cleaning the gravestone, pouring water, and offering incense and flowers.
- ⟦{樹木|じゅもく}→樹木：04955_jumoku⟧{葬|そう} (tree burial) and other non-stone alternatives have been growing in popularity, partly due to declining family sizes and the cost of maintaining traditional graves.

SIMILAR / RELATED TERMS:
- ⟦お{墓|はか}→お墓：21734_ohaka⟧: grave (the everyday word, refers to the whole grave site)
- ⟦{墓地|ぼち}→墓地：15232_bochi⟧: cemetery
- {墓標|ぼひょう}: grave marker (often a simpler wooden stake or smaller marker)
- ⟦{石碑|せきひ}→石碑：13725_sekihi⟧: stone monument (general — not necessarily a grave)
- {戒名|かいみょう}: posthumous Buddhist name (often inscribed on gravestones)
